exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Code Repositories
exploitedBy.relevance: Plaintext git protocol exposes repository data in transit, enabling unauthorized access to code repositories.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol
exploitedBy.relevance: Unencrypted git protocol can be intercepted to exfiltrate source code over an alternative, insecure protocol channel.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Downgrade Attack
exploitedBy.relevance: Directly describes forcing a connection to use a weaker TLS version, which is the core concern of this vector.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Adversary-in-the-Middle
exploitedBy.relevance: A TLS downgrade attack typically requires an adversary-in-the-middle position to intercept and manipulate the TLS handshake.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Exfiltration Over Webhook
exploitedBy.relevance: Unauthenticated webhook delivery can be abused to receive or exfiltrate data without proper identity verification.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Compromise Software Dependencies and Development Tools
exploitedBy.relevance: Unauthenticated webhooks in CI/CD pipelines can allow attackers to inject malicious events into development toolchains.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Steal or Forge Authentication Certificates
exploitedBy.relevance: Absence of mutual TLS means certificates are not required for both sides, enabling forged or stolen certificates to impersonate legitimate endpoints.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: SSH Hijacking
exploitedBy.relevance: Bypassing SSH host key verification allows an attacker to hijack SSH sessions by impersonating the legitimate server.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: SSH
exploitedBy.relevance: SSH host key verification bypass directly undermines the authentication mechanism of the SSH remote access protocol.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Forge Web Credentials
exploitedBy.relevance: Without timestamp validation, previously captured webhook payloads can be replayed as if they were freshly forged legitimate requests.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Time Based Checks
exploitedBy.relevance: Absence of timestamp validation is the failure of time-based checks that would otherwise prevent replay attacks.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Code Signing Policy Modification
exploitedBy.relevance: Lack of commit integrity verification in transit mirrors weaknesses in code signing policies that allow unsigned or tampered code to pass.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Weaken Encryption
exploitedBy.relevance: Negotiating weak cipher suites directly weakens the encryption protecting git traffic in transit.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Reduce Key Space
exploitedBy.relevance: Weak cipher suites typically involve reduced key spaces, making encrypted git traffic vulnerable to brute-force decryption.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Forced Authentication
exploitedBy.relevance: Unauthenticated LFS endpoints can be abused to force authentication credential capture from clients connecting to a rogue LFS server.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Data from Information Repositories
exploitedBy.relevance: SSRF via untrusted webhook targets can be used to access internal information repositories not otherwise reachable.
